note: The fuzzer writes the attacker-controlled input bytes (after the first decider byte) to a temporary file, which becomes the HDF5 file that will be opened.
The fuzzer calls H5Fopen on the crafted file, triggering HDF5 file parsing and superblock deserialization.
HDF5 locates the file signature at offset 0 and proceeds to load the superblock via H5AC_protect.
The metadata cache calls H5F__cache_superblock_get_initial_load_size which sets len = H5F_SUPERBLOCK_FIXED_SIZE + H5F_SUPERBLOCK_MINIMAL_VARLEN_SIZE = 9 + 7 = 16 bytes.
The initial load length is verified against the file EOA. Since the crafted file is 136 bytes, len remains 16.
A 16-byte buffer is allocated for the initial superblock image read.
The first 16 bytes of the crafted file are read into the image buffer: signature, superblock version 0, and the first 7 variable-length bytes.
The prefix decoder reads the superblock version (0) and extracts sizeof_addr=16 and sizeof_size=8 from the image buffer.
For superblock version 0, sizeof_addr is read from image[4] (offset 13 in the buffer), yielding 16. This value is used to compute the final superblock size.
sizeof_size is read from image[5] (offset 14), yielding 8. Both sizes pass the validity check (allowed values: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32).
The EOA is extended to the computed superblock size: 9 + (15 + 4*16 + H5G_SIZEOF_ENTRY(16,8)) = 9 + (15 + 64 + 48) = 136 bytes.
The final superblock size is computed as 136 bytes based on version 0, sizeof_addr=16, sizeof_size=8.
The final load size of 136 bytes is returned. Since actual_len (136) != len (16), the buffer is reallocated to 136 bytes.

code: H5F_block_read(f, type->mem_type, addr + len, actual_len - len, image + len);
note: The remaining 120 bytes of the crafted file are read into the reallocated 136-byte buffer, filling the complete superblock image.
The deserializer asserts len >= 15 (debug-only). In the release build this assert is compiled out, so no bounds check is enforced on subsequent reads.
The prefix is decoded again, confirming super_vers=0, sizeof_addr=16, sizeof_size=8. The image pointer advances to offset 9.
Skips the freespace version byte (offset 9).
Skips the root group version byte (offset 10).
Skips the reserved byte (offset 11).
Skips the shared header version byte (offset 12).
Skips the sizeof_addr byte (offset 13).
Skips the sizeof_size byte (offset 14).
Skips the reserved byte (offset 15).
Reads sym_leaf_k=4 from offsets 16-17.
Reads snode_btree_k=16 from offsets 18-19.
Reads status_flags=0 from offsets 20-23.
Reads base_addr (16 bytes) from offsets 24-39.
Reads ext_addr (16 bytes) from offsets 40-55.
Reads stored_eof (16 bytes) from offsets 56-71.
Reads driver_addr (16 bytes) from offsets 72-87. The image pointer now points to offset 88, the start of the root group entry.
The root group symbol table entry is decoded from the image buffer starting at offset 88. The entry is 48 bytes (H5G_SIZEOF_ENTRY(16,8)), ending at offset 136 which is the end of the buffer.
Reads 8 bytes (sizeof_size=8) for name_off from offsets 88-95.
Reads 16 bytes (sizeof_addr=16) for the header address from offsets 96-111.
Reads 4 bytes for the cache type from offsets 112-115. The crafted value is 1 (H5G_CACHED_STAB).
Skips 4 reserved bytes (offsets 116-119). The pointer is now at offset 120.
The cache type is H5G_CACHED_STAB (1). The assert 2*sizeof_addr <= H5G_SIZEOF_SCRATCH (32 <= 16) fails but is compiled out in release builds.
H5F_addr_decode reads 16 bytes (sizeof_addr=16) for btree_addr from offsets 120-135, which is within the buffer.
H5F_addr_decode reads 16 bytes for heap_addr starting at offset 136, which is exactly at the end of the 136-byte superblock buffer. This reads 16 bytes past the end of the allocated buffer.
The first byte read at offset 136 is past the end of the 136-byte heap-allocated image buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
